draft.title: The Five-Year Plans
card: From 1928 the Soviet government set Five-Year Plans. These were state plans that gave factories, mines and regions output targets for a set period. Gosplan, the state planning body, drew them up.
The plans put heavy industry first: coal, iron, steel, electricity and machinery. Consumer goods such as clothing and household items got far less attention.

New factories and whole cities were built, such as Magnitogorsk, a steel centre in the Urals. Output of items like steel and coal rose sharply, though many targets were set too high and figures were often exaggerated.
The human cost was high. Workers faced long hours, poor housing and harsh discipline, and forced labour, including prisoners, was used on many projects. Shortages of everyday goods continued.
draft.remember: The plans drove rapid growth in heavy industry, paid for by the hardship of ordinary people.

a.q: Which feature best describes the Five-Year Plans?
opts: Government targets that put heavy industry first
Market prices that guided how much each factory made
Plans that gave priority to clothing and household goods
Land handed to peasants to grow what they chose
a.why: The state set output targets, and heavy industry such as coal and steel came first. Consumer goods got far less attention, so the option about clothing and household goods is wrong.
a.clue: Think about who set the targets and which industries came first.

b.q: A Soviet worker in 1932 is sent to build the Magnitogorsk steelworks. Which description of life there best fits the Five-Year Plans?
opts: Long hours and poor housing while the factory was built
Comfortable homes and plentiful goods from the new industry
Freedom to leave the project and choose another employer
Short hours because the state wanted to protect workers
b.why: The plans pushed rapid building at great human cost, so workers faced long hours and poor housing. Plentiful goods is the tempting wrong answer: new industry rose, but heavy industry came first and shortages of everyday goods continued.
b.clue: Remember who paid the cost of fast industrial growth.

a.best: Government targets that put heavy industry first

b.best: Long hours and poor housing while the factory was built
